one_liner: libuv's optional Linux io_uring path for uv_fs_* calls, replacing threadpool hand-off; off by default since 1.49.
what_it_does: libuv is the C event-loop library under Node.js; its uv_fs_* calls normally run blocking syscalls on a worker threadpool. Since 1.45 the Linux backend can instead submit read/write, fsync/fdatasync, stat/fstat/lstat (and later open, close, rename, unlink, mkdir, link, symlink, ftruncate) as io_uring SQEs and complete them on the loop thread. The API is unchanged: the same uv_fs_* calls, with silent fallback to the threadpool when a path is unavailable.
how_it_is_fast: Each request becomes one io_uring submission-queue entry on a 64-entry ring created with IORING_SETUP_SQPOLL, so a kernel polling thread picks it up without a syscall and without waking a userland worker thread; completions arrive through the ring's CQ, which is registered with the loop's epoll fd. This removes the threadpool's queue lock, thread wake-up and result hand-back per request, which dominates for small, cache-hot operations.
when_to_use: Linux servers (kernel 5.13+, ideally 6.1+) doing many small uv_fs_read/uv_fs_write/uv_fs_stat calls where threadpool hand-off overhead, not the device, is the bottleneck
Programs that saturate libuv's default 4-thread pool with file requests and would otherwise raise UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE
Embedders who control process start-up and can set both the loop option and the UV_USE_IO_URING=1 environment variable
Processes that never change privileges (no setuid/setgid after loop start)
when_not_to_use: Default builds: since 1.49 file ops go to the threadpool unless the loop is configured with UV_LOOP_USE_IO_URING_SQPOLL and the env var is set, so there is nothing to gain without opting in
Processes that drop privileges with setuid(): CVE-2024-22017 showed io_uring ops kept the old credentials when the ring existed before setuid()
CPU-constrained or containerised hosts: SQPOLL runs a kernel polling thread per ring (idle timeout 10 ms) and older kernels (<5.10.186) had a 100% CPU sqpoll bug
Android, 32-bit ARM, ppc64/ppc64le and hppa below 6.1.51: io_uring is hard-disabled in source
Large-block or device-bound I/O where the syscall path is not the bottleneck; the only published number is a /dev/zero microbenchmark

integration.form: static lib | shared lib (CMake or autotools)
integration.platforms: io_uring path: Linux x86-64/aarch64 and other 64-bit arches, kernel >= 5.10.186 with IORING_FEAT_RSRC_TAGS (5.13+); libuv itself: Linux, macOS, Windows, BSDs, AIX, z/OS
integration.thread_safety: Loop and handles are not thread-safe (design.rst); one ring per loop, used from the loop thread
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same uv_fs_* API and semantics, but must be enabled per loop with uv_loop_configure(loop, UV_LOOP_USE_IO_URING_SQPOLL) plus UV_USE_IO_URING=1 in the environment

gotchas: Docs (fs.rst) say the loop option alone enables io_uring, but uv__use_io_uring() in src/unix/linux.c returns false for SQPOLL when UV_USE_IO_URING is unset, and the code comment there claims the opposite ('unset or a positive number'); in practice both the option and UV_USE_IO_URING=1 are needed

Fallback is silent: a full 64-entry ring, writes with nbufs > IOV_MAX, an old kernel, or a failed ring setup all route to the threadpool with no error, so measure before assuming the fast path is active; reads with nbufs > IOV_MAX are capped to IOV_MAX (short read)

Per-op kernel gates: close needs >= 6.1 (code constant 0x050A00 is labelled 5.16.0 but is 5.10.0, so 5.15.90+ longterm kernels also skip io_uring close), ftruncate needs 6.9, link/mkdir/rename/symlink/unlink need 5.15, cancel needs 6.0
Node.js ships the same default (threadpool) and documents UV_USE_IO_URING=1 as the opt-in; the epoll_ctl batching ring is separate and always on since 1.50
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it when the code is already on libuv (or Node.js) and you want io_uring for file ops without rewriting around liburing; use liburing directly for custom submission control, registered buffers or O_DIRECT, and SPDK when you need to bypass the kernel block layer entirely.
verified_claims_summary: The only number is in the 1.45 commit d2c31f4 and PR #3952: a reviewer saw more than 8x throughput reading small chunks from /dev/zero versus libuv's own threadpool path; no hardware, kernel, compiler or harness is given. It measures dispatch overhead, not storage throughput.
status_note: libuv is actively maintained (1.53.0 released 2026-09-24, MIT); the io_uring file path is kept and still extended (cancel support in 1.53) but has been opt-in since 1.49 after CVE-2024-22017 and SQPOLL bugs.
